title: Rorca Observability Tab Polish & Data Integrity
description: A targeted set of fixes and polish for Rorca's self-observability features — the History, Skills, Context, Stories, and Run Skills tabs. Addresses two confirmed data-integrity bugs (jsonb double-parse in workspace-drift.ts; suggestedSkills string/object dual-format handling in SpecReviewPanel), then polishes each tab with actionable install buttons, fallback metadata, elapsed time, and commit links. Background: the spec_versions jsonb double-parse was already fixed in specs.ts and SpecDetailSlideOver suggestedSkills normalization was already applied. This spec fixes the remaining instances and adds the UI polish layer on top.

userStories.title: Fix jsonb double-parse in workspace-drift.ts (violations_json + impact_json)
userStories.description: In backend/src/routes/workspace-drift.ts lines 127-128, the code calls JSON.parse(row.violations_json || '[]') and JSON.parse(row.impact_json || '[]') on JSONB columns. Because the pg driver auto-parses jsonb columns into JavaScript objects/arrays before the code ever sees them, calling JSON.parse() on an already-parsed value coerces it to the string '[object Object]' (or a mangled comma-joined string for arrays), producing 'SyntaxError: [object Object] is not valid JSON'. The '|| []' fallback makes this worse: an empty JS array [] is truthy, so JSON.parse([]) converts [] to the empty string '' and throws 'SyntaxError: Unexpected end of JSON input'. Fix: replace both JSON.parse calls with direct object use — const violations = row.violations_json ?? [] and const impactAnalysis = row.impact_json ?? []. Also update the TypeScript cast on the queryOne call from { violations_json: string; impact_json: string } to { violations_json: unknown; impact_json: unknown } to prevent regression. The GraphDriftReport type's violations and impactAnalysis fields should continue to match the actual shapes returned. No schema changes needed — the fix is purely in the deserialization layer.
acceptanceCriteria: GET /api/workspaces/:id/drift returns a valid JSON response without throwing '[object Object] is not valid JSON'
GET /api/workspaces/:id/drift returns a valid JSON response without throwing 'Unexpected end of JSON input'
violations_json and impact_json are used directly as JavaScript values without JSON.parse wrapping
The queryOne type cast for drift_reports row uses violations_json: unknown and impact_json: unknown instead of string
The existing drift report data shape (violations array, impactAnalysis array) is preserved in the response
No other places in workspace-drift.ts call JSON.parse on a DB column value

userStories.title: Fix suggestedSkills string/object dual-format in SpecReviewPanel.tsx
userStories.description: In src/panels/SpecReviewPanel.tsx, the StoryCard component renders matched skills badges (lines ~437-455). It calls skill.relevance on each entry, assuming suggestedSkills is SuggestedSkill[] (objects with name, relevance, reason). When a spec stores suggestedSkills as a plain string array (e.g. ['react-review', 'logging-fundamentals']) — which is the actual format produced by spec generation — skill.relevance is undefined on every item, the badge style comparison (skill.relevance >= 8) returns false, all badges render with the gray/low-confidence style, and the remove button uses skill.name which is also undefined causing React key warnings. Additionally, at lines ~961-973, (s.suggestedSkills ?? []).filter((sk) => sk.name !== skillName) will never filter anything when entries are strings (sk.name is always undefined). Fix: add the same toSkill() normalizer used in SpecDetailSlideOver — typeof raw === 'string' ? { name: raw } : raw — and apply it to every suggestedSkills access in SpecReviewPanel. The normalizer should be defined once at the top of the file or in a shared utility, not duplicated inline. After normalization, skill.name is always the correct string, skill.relevance is either a number or undefined (show no score if undefined), and the remove/filter logic works correctly.
acceptanceCriteria: String-format suggestedSkills entries (e.g. 'react-review') render correctly in the StoryCard badge section with the skill name visible

userStories.title: Skills tab in SpecDetailSlideOver — one-click install for not-installed skills
userStories.description: The SpecSkillsTab component (src/components/SpecDetailSlideOver.tsx ~line 209) renders a 'NOT INSTALLED — INSTALL FROM MARKETPLACE' section that is purely informational — no install button. Users have no way to act on the recommendation without navigating away. Add an Install button to each not-installed skill card. Clicking it calls POST /api/skills/install-from-sh with { name: skillName } and the current workspaceId. Show a loading spinner while installing (replace the AlertCircle icon with a Loader2 that animates). On success: move the skill to the 'INSTALLED' section (update local installedNames state to include it) and show a brief CheckCircle2 flash before settling. On error: show a small red error message below the skill card ('Install failed — try from Marketplace'). The button should be a small 'Install' text-button styled with text-accent text-[10px] hover:underline, placed after the storyCount span in the flex row. Only one install can be in-flight per skill (disable the button while loading). WorkspaceId is already a prop on SpecSkillsTab (workspaceId: string). Use the existing apiFetch helper. No new API endpoints needed — POST /api/skills/install-from-sh already exists.

userStories.title: Context tab — spec metadata fallback when no generation log exists
userStories.description: The GenerationLogTab component (src/components/SpecDetailSlideOver.tsx ~line 892) shows an empty state for specs generated before context logging was introduced (migration 046). Currently the empty state is two text paragraphs explaining the feature. This is a dead end for old specs. Replace the empty state with a fallback card that shows the spec's own metadata (from the detail prop available in SpecDetailSlideOver): model from spec.model (or 'Unknown' if absent), generatedAt formatted as a readable date, story count, and a 'Context logging not available for this spec' label. The fallback card should look like a simplified version of the GenerationLogTab's log card: a border-border rounded-lg bg-panel with a header row showing a gray Info icon, 'Generated' label, and the formatted date. Inside show: Model badge (monospace, same style as existing log card), Story count row, and the explanatory note at the bottom. The GenerationLogTab component is currently self-contained. Pass the spec detail as an optional prop: function GenerationLogTab({ specId, specDetail }: { specId: string; specDetail?: { model?: string; generatedAt?: string; storyCount?: number } }). Wire the prop in the parent render call at line 648 of SpecDetailSlideOver. The detail object is already in scope there (it's loaded at the top of the component).

userStories.title: Batch spec version history backfill — API endpoint and Settings trigger
userStories.description: The current spec version backfill (backend/src/routes/specs.ts GET /:specId/versions) only creates version 1 for a spec when that spec's History tab is opened. If a workspace has 50 specs approved before the Postgres migration, users must open each spec individually to trigger the backfill. Add a POST /api/specs/versions/backfill endpoint that: (1) accepts optional { workspaceId?: string } body, (2) scans approved/ and pending/ directories for all workspaces matching the filter (or all workspaces if no filter), (3) for each spec file found, checks if spec_versions has any row for that spec_slug using SELECT 1 FROM spec_versions WHERE spec_slug = $1 LIMIT 1, (4) if no version exists, inserts version 1 using the file content exactly as the existing on-demand backfill does (INSERT INTO spec_versions ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING), (5) returns { backfilled: number, skipped: number, errors: string[] }. Rate-limit to one call per 60 seconds per workspace. Wire a 'Backfill spec history' button in the Developer section of Settings (src/panels/SettingsPanel.tsx, the developer or system sub-tab). Button shows: loading spinner while running, then either 'Backfilled N specs' (success, green) or 'Error: ...' (red). No automatic trigger — user must click the button explicitly.

userStories.title: Run Stories tab — elapsed time and commit SHA link per story
userStories.description: The StoriesListTab component added to src/panels/RunViewPanel.tsx shows story ID, title, status dot, and pass/fail label. It is missing two pieces of information that would make it actually useful: (1) elapsed time for completed stories, and (2) a link to the git commit that the story produced. For elapsed time: the backend GET /api/pipeline/runs/:runId endpoint returns stories with started_at and finished_at columns from story_results. Calculate elapsed as finished_at - started_at and display as '1m 23s' or '45s'. If a story is in_progress (has started_at but no finished_at), show a live elapsed timer that updates every second using a useEffect interval. For commit SHA: the backend has a story_commits table. Extend the GET /api/pipeline/runs/:runId response to include commit SHA per story: LEFT JOIN story_commits sc ON sc.run_id = sr.run_id AND sc.story_id = sr.story_id, add commitSha?: string to the story result shape. In the UI, if commitSha is present, show a small external link icon next to the story ID that opens the commit URL (construct as <workspace.githubRepoUrl>/commit/<sha> if available, else just show the short SHA as a copyable code span). The commit SHA display should be 7 characters (short SHA): commitSha.slice(0, 7).
acceptanceCriteria: Each completed story row shows elapsed time formatted as Xm Ys (or just Xs if under 1 minute)
In-progress stories show a live elapsed timer that updates every second

If no GitHub repo URL is available, the short SHA is a non-linked copyable code span
Stories with no commitSha show no commit section (no empty placeholder)
The live timer useEffect is properly cleaned up on component unmount

userStories.title: Run Skills tab — show install status and navigate to Marketplace for uninstalled
userStories.description: The GET /api/pipeline/runs/:runId/skills endpoint returns skill names + frequency counts. The RunViewPanel SkillsTab (src/panels/RunViewPanel.tsx, case 'skills') renders skill chips but does not indicate whether each skill is installed or not. This means users can't tell if the skills that ran were actually available or just suggested fallbacks. Enhance the skills tab: (1) Have the frontend call GET /api/skills?workspaceId=<workspaceId> to get the installed skills list (call once on mount). (2) For each skill in the run's skill list, show: a green CheckCircle2 if installed, or an amber AlertCircle if not installed. (3) Not-installed skills get a small 'Install' text button (same style as OT-003: text-accent text-[10px] hover:underline) that calls POST /api/skills/install-from-sh. (4) Show a section header separating installed vs not-installed skills, similar to how SpecSkillsTab does it. The workspaceId is available from WorkspaceContext (useWorkspace()). Only fetch the installed skills list if the run has at least one skill. The RunViewPanel already imports useWorkspace.

userStories.title: History tab — single-version informative state (no diff available)
userStories.description: When a spec has only one version in spec_versions (which is the case for all retroactively-backfilled specs), the SpecVersionHistory component (src/components/SpecVersionHistory.tsx) shows: the version list at the top (v1 entry), and then below it: 'Select two versions above to compare' — a dead state since there's no second version to select. When only one version exists, replace the diff pane with a useful summary of that single version's content: show all stories in a list with their status (passing or not, from spec JSON's passes field) and a count of acceptance criteria. Layout: a header row 'Version 1 — [N] stories' followed by a scrollable list of story rows. Each row: story ID in monospace, story title truncated, and a 'passed' green badge or 'pending' gray badge based on story.passes. Add a small note at the bottom: 'Version history will show diffs once this spec is edited and re-approved'. This replaces the useless 'Select two versions to compare' message only when versions.length === 1. When two or more versions exist, the existing diff behavior is unchanged. The spec content is available in versions[0] from the existing API response — but it only includes storyCount, not the full story list. Extend the GET /:specId/versions response to include a stories array (id, title, passes) when the version list has exactly 1 result, to avoid a second round-trip.
